Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Decision references: 99d01496f

Evidence: Designed by the Architect on docs/servers/steward.md 'The policy core' (99d01496f), no owner choice: the domain is (account != 0, sorted label set); handlers take one &mut DomainState and only the edges module borrows two (R34's three edges); decide(&mut Store, Event) -&gt; Effects with effects as ordered batches that stop at the first failure and every waiting state having a failure row; ids from the event's random words (R36); audit records built by one constructor from the domain; machines for session, lease, request (approve only from Rendered on that channel), crossing, blame and approval channel, with the guard -&gt; rule -&gt; mutation table on the page; the server decides nothing. ### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `1bf81a55d9999b2c1f708fc6493ad502` · 2026-10-02T08:28:45Z

> The owner decided (2026-10-02) that the steward's policy is one pure Rust state machine in a no_std, unsafe-free crate, keyed by domain (account, label set) so that only R34's three control-plane edges ever see two domains; shared by the steward server and the model (replacing model/src/steward.rs); with an Elixir reference on beamlet on the host as a differential oracle in the bench's host tests; transition tables generated into the Rust dispatch, the page's Mermaid state diagrams and the Elixir clause skeletons in the wire generator's style with a drift check, while guards and effects (R37, R7/R41, R42, R40) are hand-written with a mutation each. No state-machine library or proc-macro. The full question is ./.wash/local/STEWARD0-question.md: the domain key and what lives per domain, the machines, the one decision function with effects as data and audit records derived from the key, the two embedders, the event set, the core/server boundary, what survives of model/src/steward.rs and policy.rs, the package order and needs, any owner choice. Please design it on docs/servers/steward.md (a section for the core) and write the brief at ./.wash/local/STEWARD0-implementer.md; plan node STEWARD0 exists (todo). This can run beside the init chain: it is library and model work.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `2897996b7bb8f3988b768acb33e0be43` · 2026-10-02T08:35:04Z

> Designed on docs/servers/steward.md, "The policy core" (under Interface: the docs checker fixes the ## headings), commit 99d01496f. Brief: .wash/local/STEWARD0-implementer.md. No owner choice left.
> - Domain = (account != 0, sorted label set). sshd, init and approval channels are roles. Per domain: sub-budget, sessions and leases with their name counters, pending requests and caps, blame and lockout. No domain: the manifest, the routing index, approval channels. Handlers get &mut DomainState; only the edges module borrows two domains (R34's three edges). Audit records have one constructor taking the domain; an edge's record is stamped with the labelled side.
> - decide(&mut Store, Event) -> Effects. Events carry now and random words for ids (no counter, R36). Effects are batches with tokens, run in order, stop at the first failure, and come back as one Done; every waiting state has a failure row. The server decides nothing: transport, R26 (EndLease marked ahead of admission), running batches, keyd signing.
> - Machines: session, lease, request (approve only from Rendered on that channel), crossing, blame, approval channel. The guard -> rule -> mutation table is on the page. Mutations swap entries in a Policy fn table; the shipped crate has no switch. Four become unwritable by type and are retired; three are added.
> - Gaps written as rules, from the model: leases carved from the lease domain's sub-budget, outliving the login, ended only from the sponsor's unlabelled sessions; declassify from a session carrying the label; push snapshotted at submission. Binding hash is SHA-256 via the vendored sha2.
> - Split: STEWARD0 (crate, tables, generator, model embedder; L; needs nothing), then STEWARD1 (Elixir oracle plus a bench case running Elixir on beamlet; wire's run-vectors joins it; M). The steward step now needs STEWARD1. Plan set.
> - STEWARD0's checkpoint is its tables, which I review before any code.
